messages:
Aisha: Hey team — customer A/Acct-881 reporting intermittent 401s after yesterday's API key rotation. They say ~1% of requests still fail, mostly from one Lambda in eu-west-1. Happening since 03:10 UTC.
Sam: got it. do they call our hosted API or using dedicated?
Aisha: Hosted. They rotated via the console (Key ID k_9f3a) and revoked old key. Most clients switched fine. Only that lambda saw errors.
Jen: can we get a sample failing request log? headers, times, region?
Aisha: pasted from customer logs: 
```
curl -i -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-API-Key: 2b7f..." https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 03:14:21 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": "invalid_api_key", "message": "authentication failed" }
```
Sam: header had truncated key but looks like old key value 2b7f... Are they doing env var injection into lambda at deploy time?
Aisha: customer says their deploy process writes the key into a K8s ConfigMap, then a small platform job bundles that into the lambda artifact. They rotate the config map, but their artifact build job runs on a schedule and may have cached the old value.
Kyle: hmm. so the Lambda gets a baked-in env var inside the deployment package. If they don't rebuild immediately after rotation, the function could still have old key until next deploy. explains small percentage if only that lambda version is old.
Jen: asked customer for the function's last deploy timestamp and whether they use layer to inject env at runtime.
Aisha: they replied: last deploy 2026-03-09T22:50:12Z (before rotation). They use a build pipeline that pulls config at build time, not runtime.
Sam: good catch. but why only 1% and intermittent? should be all invocations.
Kyle: maybe they have multiple versions/aliases and traffic-splitting. some invocations hit v2 (baked with new key), others v1 (old). or warm containers still using older env? but env baked into package, so all containers of that version same key. if they have multiple aliases or multiple sharded deployments, could be mixed.
Aisha: customer confirms: They run canary traffic: 5% to v1, 95% to v2. But they say errors occur from both aliases sometimes.
Jen: okay that implies some path isn't actually using header X-API-Key from env. Are they using a secrets sidecar or a runtime refresh mechanism?
Aisha: No sidecar. Just env var consumed by app startup into an in-memory variable and used for requests.
Sam: gotcha — if they updated the configmap and rebuilt one artifact but some instances have old process memory because rolling deploy was partial, and they also have a long-lived build artifact in an internal NPM-style registry that some pipelines still reference, we can get mixed traffic. But customer said they don't use internal registry.
Kyle: to be thorough, ask for request IDs from our side for failing requests so we can correlate. need X-Request-ID or Redwood headers.
Aisha: requested. customer provided our response header X-Req-ID: rwd_0a3c9b44 at 03:14:21.
Jen: pulled logs on our side: 
```
[2026-03-10T03:14:21.432Z] rwd_0a3c9b44 | auth: key_lookup failure -> key not found
[2026-03-10T03:14:21.433Z] rwd_0a3c9b44 | source: api-gw-eu-west-1-a -> client-ip 54.12.34.56
[2026-03-10T03:14:21.433Z] rwd_0a3c9b44 | user-agent: aws-lambda/Nodejs
```
Jen: confirms our side treated those as unknown key (old key revoked).
Sam: so this is definitely the client still sending old key. We should advise customer to: 1) rebuild and redeploy lambda after rotation, 2) ensure build job pulls secrets at pipeline runtime or uses runtime secret fetch.
Aisha: customer asked if we can keep the old key accepted for a grace window while they roll. They already revoked it.
Kyle: we don't accept revoked keys. but for future rotations we can recommend staged rollover: create new key, deploy clients against both (prefer new), then revoke old after everyone migrated. provide token rotation playbook.
Aisha: customer pressed: can we re-enable the old key temporarily?
Sam: ops policy: we can re-enable a key if it's within 24h and no security flags, but needs approval from Security on-call. I'll ping them.
Sam: @SecurityOnCall can we re-enable k_9f3a for 1h to help A/Acct-881 finish rollout? (they revoked accidentally before full deploy). :pray:
vault-bot: Security approval request created: INC-2026-3110 (auto).
SecurityOnCall (via vault-bot): Can you provide evidence the key was revoked accidentally and list affected assets?
Aisha: provided deploy timestamps and traffic split.
SecurityOnCall: Approved temporary re-enable for 60 minutes. Re-enabled key k_9f3a at 03:45 UTC.
Aisha: confirmed customer saw successful requests immediately after re-enable.
Customer (via Aisha): "Thanks — we deployed and confirmed. We'll follow staged rollover next time."
Jen: follow-up action items: 1) share rotation playbook with customer (doc link), 2) recommend runtime secrets (Vault K/V with short TTL or AWS SecretsManager & Lambda env var via runtime fetch), 3) propose webhook to auto-trigger rebuilds after config change.
Sam: I'll add a short KB for support: common anti-patterns (baking secrets, cached artifacts, partial canary mixes).
Kyle: also note: if customers use long-lived artifacts, suggest signing key version in artifact metadata so builds are traceable.
Aisha: closing the ticket once KB sent. final note from customer: "We want an option to delay revoke for 1h via console — UX suggestion."
